title: Metric safety layers & circuit-breaker mapping for inference alerts
content:
Purpose
This is a working note proposing a lightweight, safety-first approach for alerting on inference metrics that minimizes noisy alerts and provides deterministic rollback/circuit-breaker behavior. The goal is operator-friendly: clear escalation fences, cost controls, and safe automatic degradations for client-facing latency/cost spikes.

Principles / design goals
- Safety-first: avoid cascading automated actions that worsen user experience. Prefer staged, reversible mitigations.
- Observable intent: every circuit-breaker must be visible on dashboards with a single toggle and provenance (which rule triggered it).
- Cost-aware sampling: heavy traces or expensive queries only run when a higher-priority gate trips.
- Rollback fences: link metric regressions directly to rollout metadata (model version, route, region).

Definitions (working)
- metric_safety_layer: a named logical grouping of related metrics used to decide a mitigation (e.g., "latency-safety", "cost-safety", "model-quality-safety").
- circuit_breaker: an automated mitigation action (soft or hard) tied to a metric_safety_layer. Example: route-fallback-to-compact-model (soft), shutdown-batch-ingestion (hard).
- safety_fence: human-readable justification attached to a circuit_breaker event for postmortem / audit.
- telemetry_escrow: short-term storage of high-cardinality traces/traceshots for the period a mitigation is active to avoid long-term retention costs.

Safety layer prototypes and candidate metrics
1) latency-safety
  - p99_inference_ms (per-route, per-model): description: 99th percentile of server-side end-to-end inference time. owner: runtime-team. type: gauge.
  - tail_kv_latency_ms: description: KV cache miss tail latency. owner: serving-runtime. notes: sample at 1% normally, ramp to 25% if p99_inference_ms > threshold.
  - impact_ratio_user_halt: description: fraction of requests experiencing > 2x expected latency for a given route. used for synthetic scoring.
  Alerting (example):
    - soft: if p99_inference_ms > 1200ms for 5m AND impact_ratio_user_halt > 0.05 -> open circuit: route-degrade-soft (reduce batch size, use lower-BW kernel). Notify ops.
    - hard: if p99_inference_ms > 3000ms for 2m -> route-failover-to-legacy-hostpool.

2) cost-safety
  - token_cost_rate_usd_per_min (per-customer, per-route): rolling 10m. triggers when sudden token spend growth outpaces historical baseline. owner: finance-observability.
  - query_cost_heat_index: composite score of tokens*latency*gpu_seconds. used to gate expensive trace capture.
  Circuit behavior: throttle non-critical routes, cap burst rate, and enable compact-quantized model variants.

3) quality-safety (ML quality)
  - hallucination_flag_rate: fraction of operator-labeled outputs flagged for hallucination in last N samples. owner: ml-quality.
  - accuracy_regression_score: delta to baseline on eval prompts.
  Action: automatic rollback of model rollout if accuracy_regression_score drops below -5% on canary after 30m with >50 canary samples.

Circuit-breaker mapping (high level)
- route-degrade-soft: reduce max_batch_size by 50%, switch to smaller compilation kernels, enable prefix-caching heuristics. Visibility: dashboard flag + note with safety_fence. Manual undo allowed.
- route-failover: route traffic to fallback model variant or different region. This is automated but logged as an incident.
- telemetry-escalate: increase trace sampling for affected route to high-fidelity for a bounded window, escrow traces to telemetry_escrow.
- tenant-throttle: per-tenant rate limit cap reduction to protect shared pool.

Dashboard & UX notes
- Single pane for "Active Safety Actions" that shows: circuit_breaker_id, triggered_at, trigger_thresholds, current_state, provenance (route, model, PR/rollout id), owner, safety_fence text. Clicking opens a focused investigation panel.
- Each safety layer must have a 1 widget summary (badge style) used in oncall rotation email. Badges: green/yellow/red + reason.
- Cost amortization strip: show cost delta attributable to the mitigation (e.g., expected savings from throttling). Helps PM/finance tradeoffs.
- Compact timeline view: for each mitigation, show the metric that tripped, the mitigation enacted, and the corresponding SLI delta post-action. This is essential for evaluating automation efficacy.

Tracing and sampling strategy tied to safety layers
- Default: low trace sampling (0.1%) across inference.
- On soft safety trigger: increase sampling for the affected route to 5% for 15 minutes. Collect KV cache context + last prompt.
- On hard trigger: emergency bundle capture: 100% sampling for 30s + telemetry_escrow retention (72h). Only stored in escrow storage tagged for the incident id and auto-deleted after retention.
- Trace privacy: prior to storing, scrub PII by default using the trace-scrubber lambda. Any exceptions require an explicit data-use tag and legal review.

Example alert rules (pseudo)
- ALERT: inference_p99_high_soft
  WHEN p99_inference_ms{route="$route"} > 1200 FOR 5m
  AND impact_ratio_user_halt{route="$route"} > 0.05
  ACTIONS: annotate-dashboard, notify-#ops-alerts, open-ticket ENG-<auto>, set circuit: route-degrade-soft

- ALERT: tenant_token_spike
  WHEN token_cost_rate_usd_per_min{tenant} > baseline(tenant) * 4 FOR 10m
  ACTIONS: notify-finance, set circuit: tenant-throttle, reduce-burst-for-tenant

Operator runbook (compact)
- When an active safety action appears:
  1) Open the single-pane "Active Safety Actions". Identify provenance (rollout id / route).
  2) If canary/rollout in progress => stop rollout and roll back if quality-safety triggered.
  3) If latency/cost safety triggered: verify circuit action (soft vs hard). If soft and mitigations exist, wait 10m to see delta in SLI.
  4) If mitigations do not improve SLI within 20m OR hard trigger fired -> escalate to SRE lead, follow incident playbook.

Ownership and change control
- All circuit-breaker rules must live under a single repo (obs-rulebook) with code-reviewed changes and a test harness that replays historical telemetry to assert no flapping for known traffic patterns.
- Any new safety_fence must include: owner, intended rollback criteria, metrics used, expected user-visible impact, and cost impact estimate.

Unresolved questions / open items
- How do we safely coordinate multi-route mitigation where a single tenant spans several routes? (partial idea: tenant-level circuit that aggregates route-level triggers but requires n-route correlation).
- Telemetry_escrow privacy: do we need per-tenant escrow toggles and a legal flow for air-gapped customers?
- How to define a robust baseline for token_cost_rate_usd_per_min across tenants with irregular burst profiles? (suggest looking into median-of-week-of-day baselines).

Action items
- (Lila) prototype the single-pane Active Safety Actions dashboard (skeleton widgets) — due 2026-03-10.
- (Diego) add telemetry_escrow retention lifecycle to infra playbook and cost estimates — due 2026-03-05.
- (Rina) draft obs-rulebook PR that introduces circuit-breaker schema and test harness; include synthetic replay test — due 2026-03-12.

Notes to self
- Keep triggers conservative initially; prefer manual escalation for first 3 months.
- We should hook this into Rollouts (product/console) so the rollback fence is visible where engineers trigger canaries.

References
- See linked artifacts above for metric-contract canonical doc and the obs-rulebook PR template.

End of working draft. Feedback welcome — looking for comments on thresholds, privacy constraints, and dashboard UX copy.
